checks.label: The V-I graph is a straight line that passes through the origin, this shows that the current and voltage are proportional: every resistor line drawn from V = IR (3, 4, 5, 8 and 10 Ω) passes through (0, 0), and along each, doubling the current doubles the voltage, so 6 V at 2 A is 12 V at 4 A

If the line were not straight, then the material would not be ohmic and we would not be able to use Ohm's law: the example part's V-I curve bends, its volts per amp going from 2.5 at 2 A to 3.75 at 4 A, so no one resistance fits it and doubling 2 A gives 15 V, not 10 V

R (the slope of the V-I graph) is a constant for a given conductor and is called the resistance: with voltage up the side each resistor's line climbs R volts for every amp, so the steeper line is the one with more ohms; the 10 Ω line is drawn steeper than the 5 Ω, and line B (8 Ω) is the steepest of A (4 Ω), B and C (3 Ω)

With voltage on the y-axis and current on the x-axis: every V-I graph in the lesson puts voltage up the side, except the screens that say they have current up the side; when the axes swap, the 5 Ω line ends at (30, 6) and is steeper than the 10 Ω line ending at (30, 3), and with current up the side the line that climbs less (line B, 15 Ω, 2 A at 30 V, against line A, 6 Ω, 5 A at 30 V) has more ohms

A line that misses (0, 0) or bends is not in proportion, worked from each rule: the call-out costs £100 for 2 h and £160 for 4 h, not £200; the drum weighs 20 kg at 0 m, 30 kg at 20 m and 40 kg at 40 m, not 60 kg; the heater gives 20 W at 2 A and 80 W at 4 A, four times; the tank holds 20 cm at 0 min and 50 cm at 6 min

Each puzzle's answer is worked out from its rule: (4, 12); it misses (0, 0); 15 V; line B; (6, 2) for 3 Ω at 2 A, current up; line B, the one with more ohms, current up; the tank misses (0, 0), its side starting at 20 cm; and the measured readings' best-fit line runs within half a square of every reading, through (0, 0), with some above it and some below

Each puzzle accepts only its own answer, and each wrong answer it names is the one a slip gives: 2 added instead of doubling, the voltage kept, the curve's reading doubled or made four times, a line that runs furthest or is flattest, voltage put up the side, the ohms added to the amps, the steeper line taken as more ohms with current up the side; each straight, corner and zigzag slip is shown in the warning colour

Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture gives it away: no line through the given point, no answer point or reading, the drag point's readout says (?, ?), no line's ohms, the side not redrawn from 0, no best-fit line, nothing in the warning colour
Every screen, finished, keeps its labels inside the picture and clear of each other and its points inside the graph, for every answer, right or wrong, and wherever the reading is slid

Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion within 2.5 s and a slip within 1 s; parts start at least 0.45 s apart and counted steps at least 0.2 s apart
